label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Kiran, Appa, Amma, Divya —

First, the part you actually asked for: you're right, and I'm sorry. This has been discussed over months, and when the agent told me they needed my sponsor letter and bank statements to get the visa file together, that was the moment I should have picked up the phone and told you. Instead I carried on with the paperwork and let it reach you as a surprise in a group email on a Saturday morning. That was careless on my part, not a decision to keep you out of the loop. I'm sorry, Kiran.

Before I answer your points properly: I'm genuinely thrilled that Amma and Appa are coming. Anika has made a laminated welcome timetable — there's an entry that reads "Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays." The annexe is finished, ground floor, no steps, own shower with a grab rail. It's ready for you both.

On your three concerns:

**Appa's heart.** You're right that visitors don't get free NHS treatment, so let me be specific rather than vague. Dr. Prakash is doing a review in March before they fly and a video consult in July, and he's happy to share Appa's notes with me — I'll ask him to send a copy straight to you as well, if Appa's comfortable with that. I've also got travel insurance for the full six months, about £640 each, with pre-existing cardiac cover; the agent says it covers the stent, and I'm getting the wording in writing so all of you can read it instead of taking anyone's word for it. On the NHS side, they'll register with a local GP practice as soon as they land, and there's a visitor healthcare scheme attached to the long-stay visa that I'll confirm the details of with the practice manager. And practically: Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from the door, I work in emergency medicine there and I know half the cardiology team, so if Appa needs an echo or a review in between, it's a short drive and a familiar face rather than a stranger with a folder.

**Amma away six months.** You're right that it's the longest she's been away since Paati. What I'd say is that she can go home whenever she wants — the return ticket is flexible, we can change it with a week's notice. It doesn't have to be all or nothing, and it doesn't have to be decided today.

**Ganesh Chaturthi.** Not gone, just moved. Two ways we could do it: they fly Leicester to Pune in September and finish the trip there with you, so they're home for the festival; or the Pune lot come over here in August — and we'd cover your flights for that visit, all of you, as our treat.

One more thing. Appa, the vegetable patch was always your idea — on the phone in August, when Rohan showed it to you on video, you said "I could grow drumsticks there." That's where this started. We've only made room for it.

Can we all do a call this Sunday, 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? Appa, Amma, Kiran, Divya, Anika, Rohan — a proper conversation is better than a thread for this.

Amma, Divya says murukku achu, so please bring that as well as the pickles. We have very little excuse.

With love,
Meera
